# Errors and validation

<!-- Generated by `npm run train` from the sources each rule cites. To change a rule for good, change its source or say so in training/feedback.md; the next training run regenerates this file. -->

- **When a shared-state or session store fails, fail closed. Let the failure propagate, or wrap it in a dedicated store-unavailable exception that maps to 503. Never treat a failed read as 'not found', false or empty. Never answer 401, issue a challenge, or continue with an anonymous principal or null session. Single-use, replay and freshness checks must reject the request when the store is unreachable, and must reject an expiry that is not in the future.** Accepting a request the server cannot check lets replays through. Answering 401 to a store outage ends valid sessions and sends SPAs into login loops. *Check:* Look for catch blocks around store calls that return null/false/empty, map the failure to 401 or a challenge, clear the session, or treat the error as success. Look for single-use checks that admit on store failure or record keys whose expiry has already passed. *Note:* Rate limiting is the deliberate exception and fails open (see the rate-limiter rule). <sub>Identity ADR-0164; Identity ADR-0267; Identity ADR-0290; Identity ADR-0292; Identity docs/backend-for-frontend.md</sub>
- **Make rate limiters and quotas fail open. When the counter store throws or times out, admit the request without counting it, still record its usage meters, log a warning naming the stage, record the outcome in the rate-limiting metric, and back off from the store. Give each best-effort store call a short explicit timeout (about 100 ms) and a circuit breaker. Time the breaker with a monotonic timestamp, and close it only on an answer to a call made after it opened.** Rate limiting protects capacity, not correctness, so a cache outage must not become an authentication outage. Without a short timeout and a breaker, every request pays the client's full timeout during an outage. *Check:* Look for limiter or quota code that rejects or throws on counter-store failure, admits without logging or a metric, or retries the store on every request. Look for breakers timed with DateTime.UtcNow or TimeProvider.GetUtcNow, or that any late answer can close. <sub>Identity ADR-0196; Identity ADR-0198; Identity ADR-0246</sub>
- **Do not swallow exceptions or errors. Catch only what you can handle, and otherwise rethrow, log or turn the failure into a meaningful outcome. Never write an empty `catch` or an `async void` method.** Swallowed errors hide failures, and exceptions from async void methods cannot be observed. *Check:* Look for `catch { }`, catch blocks that only return a default value, catch-all handlers that discard the exception, ignored error results with no documented reason, and `async void` methods. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity .claude/commands/review-plan-diff.md; Identity .github/agents/copilot-reviewer.agent.md; NCodeGroup maintainer: principal-engineer-review</sub>
- **Never use `Debug.Assert` to validate untrusted input, buffer sizes or decode results. Use runtime checks that remain in Release builds.** `Debug.Assert` is compiled out of Release builds, so a wrong size or malformed input is accepted silently. *Check:* Look for `Debug.Assert` that guards decoded lengths, buffer sizes or the success of parsing externally supplied data. <sub>Identity ADR-0092</sub>
- **Treat a malformed security-relevant header as a protocol error, never as an unhandled exception or as a missing value. An undecodable client credential is `invalid_client`. A forwarded client-certificate header that is present but cannot be decoded is `invalid_request` (400), with a warning that names the header and the format. Decode such values all-or-nothing: reject the whole value if it has text around PEM blocks, empty entries, non-CERTIFICATE blocks or repeated keys. Do not hand callers a tri-state Decoded/Absent/Malformed result.** Reading malformed input as 'absent' hides proxy misconfiguration and can silently issue unbound tokens. Lenient partial parsing can accept smuggled values. *Check:* Look for credential or certificate-header parsing that throws, asserts, returns null, or falls through to the no-certificate path when decoding fails. Look for decoders that skip bad entries or let a repeated key overwrite an earlier one, and for status enums passed to consumers. <sub>Identity ADR-0092; Identity ADR-0172; Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md</sub>
- **Decode untrusted text with a strict encoding and never substitute or strip invalid characters. Catch `DecoderFallbackException` and rethrow it as the exception type the API documents, or on inbound paths map it to the protocol's error response. Check values that must be ASCII, such as tokens, explicitly (for example with `Ascii.IsValid`).** Substituted characters turn malformed input into different, valid-looking input. An uncaught DecoderFallbackException escapes the documented contract and surfaces as a 500. *Check:* Look for strict `GetString` calls on request or response bodies without DecoderFallbackException handling, catch blocks that continue with replacement characters, and ASCII-only values that are never validated. <sub>Identity ADR-0266; Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Before reading members of JSON parsed from wire input, require `ValueKind == JsonValueKind.Object`. `TryGet…` helpers on `JsonElement` must check `ValueKind` first and return false for any unacceptable value; they must never throw. Refuse a whole-number value that has a non-zero fraction, is out of range, or arrives as a string. Do not round, truncate or parse it.** `TryGetProperty` throws on a non-object, so hostile input can fault the caller. Rounding or parsing a numeric string invents a value the remote party never sent. *Check:* Look for property reads on parsed bodies, token headers or payloads with no object-kind check; `TryGet*` helpers that call throwing `Get*` methods; and `Math.Round`, `Math.Truncate`, `(int)` casts or `int.Parse` on protocol integers. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0277</sub>
- **Anchor validating regular expressions with `\z`, never `$`.** In .NET, `$` also matches before a trailing newline, so `^[a-z]+$` accepts "acme\n". *Check:* Look for validation regexes that end with `$`. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Validate a value in exactly the form its consumer reads it. Use the same parser the runtime uses, reject anything that round-trips to something other than what was written, and require canonical form for values compared verbatim (for example the host as `Uri.Host` reports it, or a media type without parameters). For URIs, require an explicit scheme, reject whitespace, and check the scheme the runtime needs (for example https for a URI that will be fetched).** Lenient parsers turn typos into different values: `10.0.0` becomes `10.0.0.0`, and `/path` becomes a file URI on Linux. A value stored in a different form is accepted but never matches or works at run time. *Check:* Look for validation that relies only on `IPAddress.TryParse`, `IPNetwork.TryParse`, `Uri.TryCreate` or ad hoc regexes that differ from the consuming parser, with no exact-form or scheme check. <sub>Identity ADR-0140; Identity ADR-0173; Identity ADR-0194; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Let caller and request cancellation propagate as `OperationCanceledException`. At endpoint or middleware boundaries, rethrow cancellation caused by `HttpContext.RequestAborted`, and never turn it into an error response, a retry or an audit write. A validator that returns failures as results must still rethrow cancellation, including cancellation an inner component caught and wrapped.** Cancellation means the client went away; it is not an invalid input or a server error. Writes made with the aborted token would fail anyway. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that convert request-aborted or caller cancellation into a failed result, an error status, a retry or a logged audit record, or that wrap it in a provider exception. *Note:* A best-effort call with its own bounded timeout (such as logout-time token revocation) may log its own timeout cancellation without failing the operation. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0167; Identity ADR-0270; Identity ADR-0273; Identity ADR-0274</sub>
- **When a write loses an optimistic-concurrency race, translate only the concurrency failure (such as `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` or the store's own stale-token check) into one store-neutral concurrency exception, and let every other save exception propagate unchanged. Management endpoints answer that exception with `412 Precondition Failed` and a problem body telling the caller to re-read and retry, never 409 or 500.** Callers should handle a lost race the same way for every store, and other failures must not be disguised as a lost race. A lost race is the same condition a stale If-Match reports. *Check:* Look for `DbUpdateConcurrencyException` leaking out of persistence, catches of broad `DbUpdateException`/`Exception` mapped to the concurrency exception, and endpoints where the concurrency exception becomes 500, 409 or another status. <sub>Identity ADR-0012; Identity ADR-0208; Identity ADR-0214</sub>
- **Never let a filter-driven bulk delete, revoke or update run with an empty filter. Give the filter DTO an `IsEmpty` guard, make the store method throw `ArgumentException` for an empty filter, return 400 from the API when every filter is missing, and include each new identifier field in the emptiness check.** An empty filter matches every row, for example every grant in a tenant. A tenant-wide purge should be a separate, explicit operation. *Check:* Look for bulk operations whose filters are all optional and are not rejected when empty, store methods that match all rows on all-null filters, and filter properties left out of IsEmpty. <sub>Identity ADR-0022; Identity ADR-0099; Identity ADR-0215</sub>
- **Clamp caller-supplied page sizes to a server-defined default and maximum. A batch-removal method takes a limit, throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` when the limit is below one, orders candidates by a stable key before applying the limit, and returns the count it removed.** An uncapped page size brings back the unbounded-result denial of service, and a stable order makes batches deterministic. *Check:* Look for limit or page-size parameters passed to the store without a cap, and for batch removals with no limit guard, no OrderBy before Take, or no returned count. <sub>Identity ADR-0019; Identity ADR-0218</sub>
- **Determine a failed precondition (duplicate, missing parent, existing dependents) by querying the store for that fact before the write, never by catching a store or InvalidOperationException and guessing the cause. Uniqueness checks must use a query that returns every current holder of the key, not a single-result or fail-closed routing lookup. Return structured failures that distinguish invalid values from conflicts, and answer 400 for invalid values before checking for 409 conflicts.** A caught exception does not reliably say which precondition failed. A lookup that returns nothing on ambiguity makes a taken key look free. *Check:* Look for catch blocks around persistence that produce 409/400/404, uniqueness checks that reuse a single-result lookup, validators that return only strings or a bool, and endpoints that report conflicts before input errors. <sub>Identity ADR-0011; Identity ADR-0015; Identity ADR-0160; Identity ADR-0195</sub>
- **When dispatching to observer, audit or broadcast handlers, wrap each handler in its own try/catch, log the failure, keep delivering to the remaining handlers, and never let the failure reach the publisher or change the HTTP response.** Observation must not change outcomes, and one faulty handler must not stop the others. *Check:* Look for dispatch loops with no per-handler try/catch, a single try/catch around the whole loop, a catch that rethrows, or audit publish calls on a request path whose exceptions can escape. <sub>Identity ADR-0047; Identity ADR-0049; Identity ADR-0205; Identity docs/audit-records.md</sub>
- **Send change notifications and cache-refresh broadcasts only after the write commits, publish from a `finally` so a failed follow-up step still announces the change, and treat the publish as best effort: log its failure and never fail the committed write.** The change is committed either way, and replicas that miss the announcement catch up through polling. Failing the response would misreport the outcome. *Check:* Look for notifications sent before SaveChanges or commit, publishes skipped when a later step throws, and publish exceptions that turn a committed write into an error response. <sub>Identity ADR-0169; Identity ADR-0205; Identity ADR-0219</sub>
- **Order side effects so that a failure cannot undo or skip a security outcome. Commit the revocation before deserializing the stored payload. Run fail-closed side calls (such as clearing an attempt counter) last, after the save, session revocation and audit, and run post-commit calls with `CancellationToken.None`. Carry the values a validator already verified on its result so later steps need no discovery or network calls that can throw.** A corrupt payload or a failing side store must not leave a session active or skip the save, the revocation or the audit. *Check:* Look for payload deserialization before a revocation is committed, counter or shared-state calls before persistence or audit, post-commit calls that use the request token, and post-handling steps that fetch metadata again. <sub>Identity ADR-0228; Identity ADR-0237; Identity ADR-0284</sub>
- **In background work, a failure must be visible and retried, and must never abort or duplicate other work. In a pass over many items or tenants, log each failing item and continue. A job handler signals failure by throwing (for example via `EnsureSuccessStatusCode`) rather than returning normally. When a job has several handlers, run them all and reschedule at most once per failed attempt. Set a 'last completed' marker only on success. A failed flush keeps its batch and retries it first, in a way that cannot apply the same batch twice.** One bad tenant must not block the others, a normal return marks the attempt as succeeded, and failures must neither lose data nor count it twice. *Check:* Look for loops where one item's exception ends the pass or is swallowed without logging, handlers that ignore non-success statuses, reschedule calls inside per-handler catch blocks, completion markers set in catch blocks, and flushes that drop drained data on failure. <sub>Identity ADR-0090; Identity ADR-0169; Identity ADR-0199; Identity ADR-0213; Identity ADR-0219; Identity ADR-0232</sub>
- **Bound every outbound dependency call. Give HTTP and remote calls a timeout and cancellation. Retry only a bounded number of times, with back-off and jitter, and handle 429 throttling from key-management or signing services. Give spawned processes (`Process.Start`/`WaitForExit`) a timeout. Make best-effort cleanup calls (such as logout-time token revocation) time-bounded, and log their failure without failing the operation.** A hanging or unbounded dependency call takes the service down with it, and throttled signers sit on the token path. *Check:* Look for HttpClient or remote calls with no timeout, unbounded or fixed-delay retry loops, KMS or signing clients with no 429 handling, process waits with no timeout, and cleanup exceptions that fail the operation. <sub>Identity ADR-0134; Identity ADR-0260; Identity ADR-0287; Identity ADR-0293; Identity docs/hosting-analysis.md; NCodeGroup maintainer: principal-engineer-review</sub>
- **When translating exceptions from a dependency, map only the specific failure the target type means. For example, map only the service's 'wrong key or ciphertext' failure to `CryptographicException`, report response-integrity failures as a retryable `IOException`, and let outages, auth and throttling errors propagate unchanged.** Callers act on the translated type. Mistaking an outage for a wrong key can cause key material to be discarded. *Check:* Look for catch blocks that convert broad RpcException, RequestFailedException or Exception into a domain exception such as CryptographicException. <sub>Identity ADR-0260</sub>
- **Report an invalid input to a validator as a result value, not an exception: mark each requirement succeeded or failed with a machine-readable failure code and a reason, treat the input as valid only when every requirement succeeded and none failed, and put the aggregated exception on the result. Throw only for infrastructure or provider failures, and rethrow those when an inner validator caught them. Likewise return a remote party's well-formed OAuth or `WWW-Authenticate` error as a value, and throw a provider exception, with the cause as inner exception, only for transport failures, timeouts, oversized or invalid bodies, or responses with neither result nor error.** Callers branch on the outcome, and errors such as `invalid_grant` are expected outcomes. Infrastructure failures must not be disguised as invalid input. *Check:* Look for validators or handlers that throw on bad input, call Fail without a code, or treat unmarked requirements as valid; code that throws on well-formed OAuth errors; and provider exceptions caught and turned into invalid-token results or thrown without the inner exception. <sub>Identity ADR-0120; Identity ADR-0167; Identity ADR-0270; Identity ADR-0273; Identity ADR-0274; Identity ADR-0299</sub>
- **Branch on why something failed using its machine-readable code, never by matching message text. Set the code where the failure is detected (`context.Fail(code, reason)`, or a requirement that declares its code explicitly) and never infer it later from a claim name, message or requirement type. When comparing violations before and after a change, match on structured identifying fields (subject, offending value, governing setting), not descriptions. Consumers of open error-code vocabularies must have a fallback for unknown codes.** Message text is not a stable contract, only the detecting code knows the exact reason, and replacement implementations may report codes the consumer does not know. *Check:* Look for Contains/StartsWith/regex/equality on Message or FailureReason used to branch, codes derived from names, assertions that return false without first calling Fail, diffs keyed by description, and switches over error codes with no default branch. <sub>Identity ADR-0236; Identity ADR-0240; Identity ADR-0278; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Use `InvalidOperationException` for configuration errors found at call time: an unknown strategy name, no usable or a mismatched credential, a missing key ring, or an operation the provider does not support. Keep these separate from protocol or provider exceptions, and report expected runtime failures through a result type with a status and reason. When a required security feature (such as DPoP) cannot be satisfied, fail before sending anything and never fall back to sending without it.** This separates misconfiguration from runtime conditions callers must handle, and prevents requests that are silently unbound. *Check:* Look for configuration errors reported as provider exceptions or result values, expected runtime failures that throw, and required-feature paths that skip the feature and send anyway. <sub>Identity ADR-0270; Identity ADR-0286; Identity ADR-0288; Identity ADR-0291</sub>
- **Reject input that names an unregistered or empty vocabulary member (strategy, profile, algorithm, auth method) instead of ignoring it, returning a no-op, or using a default branch. A lookup by a non-empty unknown name throws an error that includes the name. Leave an unknown hash algorithm to the framework's `CryptographicException`, and fail deprecated algorithms (such as RSA1_5) with the same generic unsupported-algorithm error as any other unregistered one, with no silent fallback algorithm.** Ignoring an unknown name fails open: the intended behavior, such as a security profile's requirements, is silently not applied. *Check:* Look for name lookups that return null or a default for unknown names, validation that accepts an empty string or any string for an enumerated value, default branches that pick a fallback algorithm, and special-case messages for deprecated algorithms. <sub>Identity ADR-0140; Identity ADR-0145; Identity ADR-0150; Identity ADR-0190; Identity ADR-0282</sub>
- **Build a registry or catalog of named descriptors or handlers once, at construction, and validate the whole set then. Reject empty or whitespace names, duplicate names, two handlers claiming the same role, missing required members, references to unregistered members, cycles and reserved names, with an `InvalidOperationException` that names the offending descriptor. Compare and sort names ordinally. Validate caller-supplied descriptor collections the same way, throwing `ArgumentException` for null entries or duplicates.** Conflicting registrations from many packages fail fast with a clear message instead of producing ambiguous behavior on each request. *Check:* Look for catalogs rebuilt or scanned on each call, first-match lookups, dictionary indexer assignment that overwrites duplicates, culture-sensitive or case-insensitive name comparers, and errors that do not name the descriptor. <sub>Identity ADR-0150; Identity ADR-0190; Identity ADR-0201; Identity ADR-0207; Identity ADR-0246; Identity ADR-0281</sub>
- **Reject values that cannot be served when they are configured or written, not when a request later uses them. Give options with constrained values (URLs, patterns, routes, codes, ranges) an `IValidateOptions<T>` or validation delegate. Validate list options in their setter where practical, and check names or keys against their storage constraints when they are first accepted.** A request-time failure reaches relying parties instead of the operator, and a bad name would otherwise fail at every background flush. *Check:* Look for new constrained options registered without validation, checks of configuration or stored data that run only in request handling, and record or enqueue APIs that accept names without checking length or characters. <sub>Identity ADR-0137; Identity ADR-0160; Identity ADR-0199; Identity ADR-0273</sub>
- **Implement each validation rule, including cross-field relations, once in a shared validator, and call it from every entry point: configuration at startup and on reload, management API writes, registration, import, seeders and deserialization of stored documents. Do not copy rules inline into individual callers, and do not resolve the services that consume the options inside an options validator.** A rule that exists only for configuration lets the API store exactly what startup refuses, and copies of a rule drift apart. *Check:* Look for validation logic duplicated between options validators and request validators, relation checks inline in one caller, and new write paths that skip validation an existing path already performs. <sub>Identity ADR-0140; Identity ADR-0159; Identity ADR-0160; Identity ADR-0206; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Make validation and startup failures actionable. Name the configuration section, options type, key and actual value of each failure. Report every failure, not just the first. Log one error per offending item, and make the startup exception list them all and name the setting or command that repairs them.** An operator should be able to fix every problem from a single failure report and one restart, without reading the code. *Check:* Look for validators that return on the first failure, messages missing the key, type or value, and startup exceptions that do not list the failing IDs or the recovery setting. <sub>Identity ADR-0137; Identity ADR-0221; Identity ADR-0247; Identity ADR-0287</sub>
- **On every write path (create, update, patch, provisioning), apply defaults for omitted values first and then run the same validation used for explicit values. For JSON Patch, apply the patch to a throwaway copy and validate the patched state before persisting anything.** A derived or patched value must be judged exactly like a supplied one, or it can produce an unservable or colliding value. *Check:* Look for defaults filled in after validation, defaulting applied on only some write paths, and PATCH handlers that validate the original entity or persist before validating. <sub>Identity ADR-0015; Identity ADR-0165</sub>
- **Never normalize a write by silently dropping input it does not support. Return 400 with a validation problem whose errors are keyed by field or setting name, covering non-object documents, unregistered names, wrong types and null for a setting with no default, and store nothing.** A write that drops part of its input and reports success hides a configuration mistake, and an accepted wrong-typed value later breaks every request that resolves it. *Check:* Look for handlers that filter out unsupported fields and return success, coerce a non-object document to `{}`, or return errors not keyed by name. <sub>Identity ADR-0139; Identity ADR-0149</sub>
- **Validate updates incrementally. Re-check a field's rules only when the update changes that field. Run per-value domain checks before relational rules. Base the 're-run this rule' gate on the inputs each rule declares. Refuse a change only for the violations it introduces, by comparing before and after.** Records written under earlier rules must stay editable, and an already-incoherent entity must not block an unrelated change. A hand-written gate can miss an input the rule reads. *Check:* Look for update validators that re-run every rule on every update, relational checks that run before or without domain checks, per-rule gates that duplicate the inputs, and refusals for violations that already existed. <sub>Identity ADR-0160; Identity ADR-0206; Identity ADR-0240</sub>
- **Cap a validation problem response at a fixed number of errors per key, with a summary error that counts the rest, while still evaluating every item.** A walk over many entities can otherwise produce an unbounded response, and the count must stay exact. *Check:* Look for responses that add one error per entity with no limit, or that stop evaluating early so the count is wrong. <sub>Identity ADR-0206</sub>
- **Fail closed on stored data a request needs. When a stored document contains an invalid entry, fail the load rather than skipping that entry. Do not catch-and-continue past stored data that feeds a read response, a policy decision or a dependent write. Throw a `JsonException`-derived exception that names the scope and owner. HTTP APIs answer it with 409 Conflict and an RFC 9457 problem body whose `detail` names the resource and the fix, with the identifiers as extensions, never 500 or 422.** Skipping data answers with values the owner does not actually have and hides the problem. 409 says the caller can repair the stored state. *Check:* Look for load paths that log and skip invalid entries, catch-and-continue around reads that feed results, generic exceptions without scope or owner, and invalid stored data escaping as 500 or mapped to 422, or a 409 sent without a problem body. *Note:* The stored-data rule below lists the cases where skipping or falling back is correct. <sub>Identity ADR-0140; Identity ADR-0149; Identity ADR-0204; Identity ADR-0245</sub>
- **Tolerate unreadable stored data only where it does not feed the result. A write that replaces an unreadable document proceeds: skip only the checks that compare against the old document, and still validate the incoming one. Write validation that walks other stored documents catches the specific exception, logs a warning, and continues. An unreadable record that only serves as an optimization is logged with a dedicated event and treated as absent. A list response omits a best-effort derived field rather than failing. Report a parse failure in its own error field, never as a fake violation with placeholder names.** Otherwise one unreadable document blocks every write, including the write that would repair it, and the operator cannot list resources to find it. *Check:* Check that the try/catch wraps only the resolution of the old or stored document and not the written one, that walks do not escape as 500, that list endpoints do not return 409 for a derived field, and that parse exceptions are not turned into violation entries. <sub>Identity ADR-0233; Identity ADR-0234; Identity ADR-0241; Identity ADR-0289</sub>
- **Treat a stored record payload that fails to decrypt as absent and log a warning, with no plaintext fallback and no 500. Do not silently delete and regenerate a persisted key that can no longer be decrypted: outside Development, fail with a message naming the owner and the lost protection key, and refuse to start when the ASP.NET Core Data Protection key ring holds a live key that cannot be decrypted.** Treating the record as absent means a forged or foreign row never authorizes anything. Quietly regenerating keys hides a lost key ring, signs users out, and changes the keys relying parties trust. *Check:* Look for decryption of stored records that propagates CryptographicException or falls back to plaintext, and for catch blocks around key unprotection or IKey.Descriptor that regenerate, drop or ignore the key in non-Development code. *Note:* Development-only seeding may regenerate a secret that can't be unprotected so the dev server stays runnable (ADR-0021). <sub>Identity ADR-0021; Identity ADR-0169; Identity ADR-0247; Identity ADR-0265</sub>
- **When a value that security identity depends on is missing, fail closed. For example, when no issuer is configured or stored, fail with an error naming the setting to configure, and never derive it from the request host. Treat a missing family start time on a refresh grant as `DateTimeOffset.MinValue`, so the horizon check refuses it.** An entity without authoritative identity must not be served under an address someone else picked, and a missing bound must not mean unlimited. *Check:* Look for null-coalescing or fallback branches that substitute request-derived or ambient values for a missing stored identity, and for horizon or expiry checks skipped when the start value is missing. <sub>Identity ADR-0100; Identity ADR-0165; Identity ADR-0182; Identity ADR-0297</sub>
- **Surface the specific reason for a refusal. Do not wrap specific validation failures (status code, content type, size) in a generic 'failed to fetch' error. Return the validator's reason in the 400 problem for a refused import. Name a missing required claim, and give an error code plus the violated requirement for a refused password.** A generic message hides the real cause from callers and from diagnostics. *Check:* Look for broad catches that replace specific errors with a generic one, failure paths that drop the validator's reason, and required-claim or password checks that fail without naming what is missing. <sub>Identity ADR-0111; Identity ADR-0186; Identity ADR-0187; Identity ADR-0236</sub>
- **Keep secrets and tokens out of error and audit messages, and give each error a stable, machine-readable code (the OAuth error code where one applies). Give a token decryption failure its own code, distinct from a signature failure, and a fixed message.** Messages are forwarded to log sinks, and operators filter on the code. *Check:* Look for messages that interpolate tokens, secrets or exception text that contains them, codes built from free text, and decryption errors mapped to the signature-failure code. <sub>Identity docs/audit-records.md; Identity ADR-0280</sub>
- **Select the handler for a polymorphic payload from an explicit type discriminator, not by trying one parser or algorithm after another and catching exceptions.** Using exceptions to guess the type is fragile and nondeterministic. *Check:* Look for try/catch chains that try one format (for example RSA, then ECC), swallow the failure and fall through to the next. <sub>Identity ADR-0105</sub>
- **Reject with 400 a request where a security-relevant single-valued query or form parameter (a guard, a return URL, a logout_token) appears more than once.** Repeated parameters are ambiguous and can be used to slip past validation. *Check:* Look for handlers that read such parameters by first value or joined value without checking that the count is exactly one, or at most one. <sub>Identity ADR-0293</sub>
- **Under a `where T : notnull` (or unconstrained) generic, never detect presence by testing a `T?` field or parameter against null. Track presence with an explicit bool, or constrain T to `struct` and use `Nullable<T>`.** For value types, `T?` there is just `T`, so the null check always reports a value and `default(T)` is used by mistake. *Check:* Look for generic types that use `x is null`/`is not null`/`!= null` on a `T?` member to decide whether a value exists. <sub>Identity ADR-0010; Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Never use the null-forgiving operator `!`, even with a justification comment. Restructure so the compiler proves the value is non-null (`?? throw`, `[MemberNotNullWhen]`, `is { } x`, early return). Declare locals that receive `[MaybeNullWhen(false)]` out arguments as nullable, and in tests narrow a maybe-null value with `Assert.NotNull` before dereferencing it.** Nullable warnings are errors, and `!` suppresses the check instead of fixing the cause. *Check:* Look for any postfix `!` (including `null!` and ones annotated `// !`), non-nullable locals receiving MaybeNullWhen out values, and test dereferences without a prior Assert.NotNull. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md; Identity ADR-0127</sub>
- **Null-guard the receiver of an extension member with `ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull` or an equivalent guard. When throwing an `ArgumentException` about the receiver, pass `nameof(receiver)` as paramName and suppress CA2208 with a tight `#pragma warning disable/restore` and a one-line reason.** Extension members can be invoked on null, and CA2208 does not yet treat an extension-block receiver as a parameter. *Check:* Look for extension members that dereference the receiver unguarded, receiver exceptions with no paramName, and broad or unexplained CA2208 suppressions. <sub>Identity csharp-production.instructions.md</sub>
- **Do not fall back to `DateTime` parsing when a `DateTimeOffset` parse fails. When adding a margin or skew to an externally supplied instant, use saturating arithmetic that clamps at `DateTimeOffset.MaxValue`/`MinValue`.** The fallback silently produces a wrong, machine-local instant, and plain addition near the end of the range overflows into a server error. *Check:* Look for DateTimeOffset-then-DateTime parse chains, and `+`/`Add` of a TimeSpan to token- or request-derived times without clamping. <sub>Identity ADR-0121; Identity ADR-0123</sub>
- **Validate numeric bounds explicitly. Throw `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for a required lifetime or timeout `TimeSpan` that is not positive. Reject negative retention values but accept zero when it means immediate removal.** Unbounded sessions or nonsensical retention must not be possible, while legitimate edge values stay usable. *Check:* Look for lifetime or timeout parameters that accept zero or negative values, and retention validators that allow negative values or reject zero. <sub>Identity ADR-0220; Identity ADR-0221</sub>
- **When treating a value as a list by testing for `IEnumerable`, exclude `string` first, and compare elements with default (ordinal) equality.** A string is an `IEnumerable<char>` and must be compared as a scalar. *Check:* Look for `is IEnumerable` checks without a preceding string exclusion, and culture-sensitive or case-insensitive element comparison. <sub>Identity ADR-0240</sub>
- **Validate inputs and configuration before requesting a named client from `IHttpClientFactory`, so that handler-building callbacks only look up values that are already validated and cannot throw configuration errors.** IHttpClientFactory caches an exception thrown while building a named handler, so the error outlives its fix. *Check:* Look for code inside ConfigurePrimaryHttpMessageHandler or IConfigureNamedOptions<HttpClientFactoryOptions> that can throw on bad configuration. <sub>Identity ADR-0288</sub>
- **A `TryGet…(…, out …)` probe used on a hot path (for example before a cache lookup) must not throw and must not do I/O. It returns false when the answer cannot be worked out cheaply, and authoritative validation stays in the full load path.** The probe exists to avoid the store read, and throwing or doing I/O in it defeats that purpose and blurs where validation happens. *Check:* Look for Try-pattern probes that call a store, await I/O or throw validation exceptions, and for validation moved from the full load method into the probe. <sub>Identity ADR-0037</sub>
- **A validation handler chained after others must return immediately when the operation already has an error, and must never overwrite that error.** An earlier refusal must stand as it is. *Check:* Look for later-priority handlers that do work or set an error without first checking for an existing one. <sub>Identity ADR-0224</sub>
- **In authentication handlers, a missing or invalid bearer token leaves the principal anonymous so downstream authorization returns 401 or 403. Once a client-authentication handler owns a request, a missing or mismatched credential is a conclusive `invalid_client` and must not fall through to other handlers or anonymous handling.** Authentication only populates the principal and must not add a second enforcement path, but a client that registered a method must not be able to bypass it. *Check:* Look for authentication steps that write their own error responses for missing bearer tokens, and for owned client-auth paths that return 'not handled' on failure. <sub>Identity ADR-0044; Identity ADR-0107</sub>
- **Classify OAuth and upstream-provider failures consistently. Unreachable or unreadable metadata, keys or token endpoints, HTTP errors, and timeouts the caller did not cause are 'provider unavailable', never invalid credentials. On refresh, only `invalid_grant` ends the session (401); other OAuth errors answer 502; transport failures and timeouts answer 503. On the server side, use `invalid_request` for refusals the client can fix and `server_error` for unsatisfiable server configuration, never an unhandled exception.** Outages must not end user sessions or be reported as the client's fault, and configuration faults must not blame the client. *Check:* Look for HttpRequestException or timeouts treated as authentication failures, refresh handling that ends sessions on transient errors or collapses all failures into one status, and missing-key exceptions that escape unhandled. <sub>Identity ADR-0158; Identity ADR-0290; Identity ADR-0291</sub>
- **Never redirect an error to a `redirect_uri` that cannot be trusted. Return failures to resolve a pushed `request_uri` directly as 400. Select response-securing keys and algorithms before the user authenticates or a code is issued, and report a selection failure as a non-redirected `server_error`.** If the request could not be recovered or the response cannot be secured, no redirect target can be trusted, and no code should be issued for it. *Check:* Look for request_uri failures sent through the redirect error path, and for key or algorithm selection done inside the response handler or after authentication. <sub>Identity ADR-0089; Identity ADR-0201</sub>
- **Validate client registrations and settings writes against server capabilities and internal consistency, using `invalid_client_metadata`. Reject response types whose grant type is not registered, unsupported grant or response types, settings that need a disabled server capability, algorithms outside the effective `*_values_supported` ceiling, and redirect URI kinds (including `post_logout_redirect_uris`) the settings disallow. Recheck at request or issuance time, and refuse settings changes that would leave a stored client invalid.** What the server does must match what it advertises, and settings can change after a registration was written. *Check:* Look for registration or management paths that store values without these checks, issuance that trusts stored algorithms without rechecking them, and settings updates that skip revalidating stored clients. *Note:* Do not reject a registered grant type just because no response type uses it (RFC 7591, OpenID Connect Registration). <sub>Identity ADR-0088; Identity ADR-0141; Identity ADR-0155; Identity ADR-0203</sub>
- **Enforce PKCE strictly. At the authorization endpoint, reject a `code_challenge_method` outside the supported set. At the token endpoint, answer `invalid_grant` for a method with no registered transformation, with no default method. Validate a `code_verifier` when it is constructed: 43–128 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9-._~]` (RFC 7636 §4.1).** Silently accepting unknown methods or invalid verifiers weakens the advertised PKCE guarantee. *Check:* Look for PKCE code that falls back to a default method, uses another error code, or builds verifiers without checking length and character set. <sub>Identity ADR-0079; Identity ADR-0275</sub>
- **Make JWK Set handling robust but fail closed. When importing a fetched set, skip a key with a missing, empty or unsupported `kty` or malformed material, using the single-key validity test, instead of failing the whole set. When fetching a remote `jwks_uri` fails, log a warning and verify against only the locally known keys; never throw out of the resolver or skip verification. When exporting a key type with no registered exporter, fail clearly instead of emitting a partial key.** One bad key must not break a usable set, a fetch error must never become an authentication bypass, and a partial key representation could be trusted by a relying party. *Check:* Look for set-import loops that throw on one bad member, key resolvers that propagate fetch exceptions or return permissive results, and export code that skips unknown key types or emits null members. <sub>Identity ADR-0058; Identity ADR-0106; Identity ADR-0281</sub>
- **Validate JWK metadata on both import and update. Each key in a set needs a `kid` unique within the set and among the owner's keys. `use` is `sig` or `enc`. `key_ops` holds distinct values that agree with `use`. `alg` is registered, matches the use, and accepts the key's type and size. Request values may repeat the JWK's `kid`, `use` or `alg` but must not contradict them. An update keeps the existing `kid`. Sign and verify must throw `ArgumentException` on a curve mismatch, and a JWK constructor must throw when the given type descriptor differs from `kty`.** Key selection depends on `kid` (OpenID Connect Core §10.1.1), RFC 7517 §4.3 requires `use` and `key_ops` to agree, and a mismatched key must never produce or accept a signature. *Check:* Look for import or update paths that skip the kid-uniqueness, use/key_ops/alg or algorithm-to-key-type checks, silently override JWK metadata from the request, drop the KeyId on update, or sign without a curve check. <sub>Identity ADR-0161; Identity ADR-0186; Identity ADR-0271; Identity ADR-0272</sub>
- **When a claim value is malformed, out of range or unrepresentable for its declared type (including NaN/Infinity doubles), emit it as its verbatim string. Never throw and never coerce it to a different type.** Throwing turns one malformed claim into a failed token issuance, while the verbatim string keeps the data. *Check:* Look for claim encoding that uses Parse instead of TryParse, serializes non-finite doubles, or calls JsonDocument.Parse without a fallback. <sub>Identity ADR-0122</sub>
- **For X.509 handling, choose the key's own certificate from a collection by `HasPrivateKey`, not by position, and throw `ArgumentException` when no certificate or more than one certificate has a private key. When a nested revocation check (of a CRL signer or delegated responder) is not `Good`, treat the evidence as unusable, never as `Revoked` for the end certificate.** PKCS#12 does not order its bags, and the signer's status only decides whether the evidence can be trusted. *Check:* Look for `collection[0]` or `First()` used as the key certificate, silent acceptance of zero or several private-key certificates, and nested Unknown or Revoked results propagated as Revoked. <sub>Identity ADR-0259; Identity ADR-0300</sub>
- **When a management endpoint depends on a service from an optional, opt-in package that is not registered, respond 501 Not Implemented, not 500 or 404.** A missing registration means an unsupported capability, not a server fault. *Check:* Look for endpoints that resolve an optional service and throw, or return 500 or 404, when it is absent. <sub>Identity ADR-0057</sub>
- **When an exception handler can be customized per endpoint, resolve it per request from the endpoint's metadata first, then from the DI-registered default.** Individual endpoints can customize error rendering while all the others keep the shared default. *Check:* Look for handler resolution that ignores endpoint metadata or reverses the order. <sub>Identity ADR-0009</sub>
- **Handle validation, errors, edge cases and logging the same way in code paths meant to be equivalent (sibling modules, read/write, encode/decode, sync/async overloads), and cover failure modes, null/empty/boundary inputs and invariants all the way down to the low-level code, not just the happy path.** An asymmetric or happy-path-only implementation delivers the capability inconsistently, and closing those gaps is part of the capability, not new scope. *Check:* Compare each changed method with its counterparts for a validation, exception, edge case or log event that one has and the other lacks. Trace each capability into its low-level methods for unvalidated inputs and invariants that are assumed but never enforced. <sub>NCodeGroup maintainer: gap-hunting-review; NCodeGroup maintainer: principal-engineer-review</sub>
- **In automation scripts, distinguish an expected 'not found' result from other failures by its specific exit code (for example `git ls-remote --exit-code` returning 2), and fail the job on any other error.** A network error was once reported to users as a missing release line. *Check:* Look for scripts that treat any non-zero exit code as one specific expected condition. <sub>Identity review of #420</sub>
- **Make Helm charts fail at render time (`fail`/`required`) for configuration the application would refuse at startup or that cannot run safely, such as wildcard allowed hosts, a missing required Secret, or multiple replicas without shared state.** `helm install` then fails before anything is applied, instead of leaving a pod in a crash loop. *Check:* Look for new application startup validations or unsafe combinations that have no matching render-time failure in the chart templates. <sub>Identity ADR-0179</sub>
